genome.summary: Resolve late orders by policy; escalate only when policy requires

gen2.summary: Resolve late orders by policy; escalate only when policy requires

result.headline: Ship gen2: 91% vs 69% for gen1, 99.8% chance to win.
reasons: resolved: gen2 91% vs 69% for gen1 (lift +32%, 95% CI +10% … +53%, 99.8% chance to win)

gen2.hypothesis: If gen2 resolves late-delivery cases (including 'get me a human' requests) by policy and stops offering escalations the policy doesn't require, the resolved rate rises from 73% to about 85% and escalations fall from 25% to under 10%, because 17 of the 24 failures were unnecessary handoffs on cases the policy fully covers.
gen2.expected_effect: Resolved: roughly +10 to +15 points. Escalated: down from 25% to around 8–12% (refunds over $500 and customers who insist remain). Cost per chat: roughly flat to +15%. The longer prompt adds input tokens, but fewer escalation turns and fewer get_policy calls (key rules are now in the prompt) partly offset that, staying well under the +30% cap.

genome.name: gen3
genome.summary: Create returns without asking reason; no escalation invites; low effort

gen3.summary: Create returns without asking reason; no escalation invites; low effort
gen3.hypothesis: If ShopBot creates returns without asking for a reason (defaulting to "other"), stops inviting escalation, skips get_policy for covered topics, and runs at low effort, then cost per chat falls by at least 30% and resolution rises, because the drop-offs and unneeded handoffs seen in 7 of 7 failures disappear while fewer tool calls, turns and reasoning tokens are used.
gen3.expected_effect: Resolved rises from about 91% toward 96% or more as the return-reason drop-offs are removed. Escalated falls from about 5% toward 1–2%, since the remaining handoffs should only be refunds over $500 or explicit repeat requests. Cost per chat falls about 30–45%, driven by low effort, fewer get_policy calls and fewer turns per chat.

result.headline: Ship gen3: cost per chat $0.00067 vs $0.00073 for gen2 (-8%), 99.7% chance it's lower.
reasons: gen3: cost per chat $0.00067 vs $0.00073 for gen2 (-8%, 95% CI -14% … -2%, 99.7% chance it's lower)

genome.name: gen5
genome.summary: Resolve human demands by policy first; no escalation offers

gen5.summary: Resolve human demands by policy first; no escalation offers
gen5.hypothesis: If the prompt restores 'escalate only when policy requires; resolve demands for a human by policy first; never offer escalation' and states the late-delivery tiers, the resolved rate rises from 94% toward 98%+ and escalations drop. The failures are all policy-resolvable late orders that were handed off.
gen5.expected_effect: Resolved up about 4–5 points, to about 98–99%. Escalated down from 13% to about 6–8%, leaving only policy-required handoffs such as refunds over $500. Cost per chat up roughly 10–20% from the longer prompt and the extra lookup/credit calls in former instant-escalation chats, partly offset by fewer get_policy calls for late orders. This stays within the 30% cap.
